reader.notes: Re-read on this branch (kb/Work PB2627) at the pin: the aligned CobolIntrinsics.OrdMax/OrdMin(params Int128[]) are deleted, and no program reached them (on main the renderer's ORD-MAX/ORD-MIN arms already named OrdMaxAt/OrdMinAt, the string pair and the exact, wide and decimal bodies, and RealMethod named OrdMaxReal). The catalog row no longer names a runtime member; the renderer keys the selection set on sig.Name (MAX, MIN, ORD-MAX, ORD-MIN, MEDIAN) and names each body through a nameof-anchored RuntimeApi.IntrinsicBody constant, the binary64 body through Binary64Bodies. Every carrier selects through the one kernel Selection.cs#ExtremeIndex: start at index 0, replace only on a strictly greater (or strictly smaller) comparison, so the leftmost of equal values stands (RV3), and return index + 1 (RV1). Each carrier supplies its simple-condition comparison (RV2): ScaledOrder through CobolNum.Compare (by value, not scale), ExactOrder through CobolExact.Compare, ValueOrder for binary64, StringOrder through the program collating sequence with space extension, WideOrder through CobolWide.Compare. The wide lane was not reached by an 85 probe here; its body is the same one-line call of the kernel.
reader.requirement: On a tie for the greatest value FUNCTION ORD-MAX returns the position of the leftmost argument-1 having that value, for numeric arguments of any scale and sign and for alphabetic and alphanumeric arguments.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f38_06 is numeric; the probes add scale-differing ties, -0 against 0, 18-digit operands, ALL over a table with a tie, alphanumeric ties and the exact and binary64 lanes.

refuter.evidence: Code read independently at the pin: before this branch, on origin/main, the renderer keyed the selection set on sig.RuntimeMethod ('OrdMax'/'OrdMin') and emitted OrdMaxAt/OrdMinAt, OrdMaxString/OrdMinString, the exact, wide and decimal bodies, and OrdMaxReal through RealMethod; the deleted OrdMax/OrdMin(params Int128[]) had no emitter. On the branch the same set is keyed on sig.Name with '&& !ic.ComparesStrings' added, which a string list never needed (SelectionNeedsExactLane is false for it), and the binary64 body is Binary64Bodies['ORD-MAX'] = OrdMaxReal, the same name RealMethod derived. Each body is a one-line call of ExtremeIndex with its ISelectionOrder; the kernel replaces only on a strict comparison and returns index + 1. A grep of the selection path for Edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion finds none. Attacks past the reader's probes at --std 85: y1_ord_attack.cob under PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS REV (Z Y X C B A) printed Y1 0001 for ORD-MAX('A' 'Z' 'B') and Y2 0002 for ORD-MIN (the collating sequence, not the native one, decides RV2); Y3 0003 and Y4 0001 for a numeric-edited item against alphanumeric items (class alphanumeric, compared as nonnumeric operands, an equal pair resolved leftmost); Y5 0002 and Y6 0001 for OE(ALL) of an ODO table with OC = 3 holding -1.5, 2.0, 2 (the series bounded by the ODO object, the scale-differing tie leftmost); Y7 0001 for ORD-MAX(D1 OE(ALL) 2) + 0 (a table expanded inside a longer list); Y8 COND for ORD-MIN(3 2 1) = 3 in a condition.
